title: The Maze II
statement: Find the shortest rolling route. start and destination are distinct in-bounds empty [row,column] cells; at least two empty cells exist. The ball rolls to a wall or outside border before it can turn. It must STOP at the destination, not merely pass through it. Minimize traveled cells, excluding the start and including the destination. Return -1 if stopping there is impossible.
constraints: 1 <= rows, columns <= 100; rectangular maze values are 0 (empty) or 1 (wall).
start and destination are distinct in-bounds empty [row,column] cells; at least two empty cells exist.
The ball rolls to a wall or outside border before it can turn. It must STOP at the destination, not merely pass through it.
Minimize traveled cells, excluding the start and including the destination. Return -1 if stopping there is impossible.
hints: Only stopping positions are states where you may choose another direction.
A roll is an edge weighted by how many cells it crosses, so use a weighted shortest-path search.
Pop the smallest distance; roll in all four directions to a wall; relax endpoint distances by the number of crossed cells.
Skip stale heap entries and zero-length moves. Accept the destination only as a popped stopping state, never while the ball passes through it.
editorial: Dijkstra applies because every nonempty roll has positive weight. A FIFO BFS minimizes roll count, not cell distance. Different paths can revisit an endpoint with a shorter distance, so a simple visited-on-discovery set is insufficient. The independent oracle constructs directional rays and uses synchronous Bellman-Ford. For V=rows*columns, scanning four rays at each endpoint costs O(V*(rows+columns)); heap operations add O(V log V). Unlike the existing Maze reachability task, the output must be the minimum travel distance.

tests.explanation: One optimal route travels left 1, down 1, left 3, down 1, right 2, down 2, right 2: 12 cells in total, not seven rolls.
Return -1. A roll can cross [3,2] but cannot stop there; ordinary one-cell-at-a-time pathfinding would incorrectly accept it.
